questions.question: A React component re-sorts a 10,000-row product list on every render though its inputs rarely change; a hook caches the result until its deps change. Which hook?
questions.explanation: useMemo memoizes an expensive computed value and recomputes only when its dependency array changes.

questions.question: A React.memo child keeps re-rendering because it receives a fresh inline handler each parent render; a hook memoizes the function's identity. Which hook?
questions.explanation: useCallback returns a stable function reference across renders, preserving prop equality for memoized children.

questions.question: Clicking 'Add to Cart' updates the badge automatically — no manual DOM work — because Angular re-checks bindings and refreshes the view after async events. What mechanism is this?
questions.explanation: Change detection compares bound model values and updates the view, typically triggered by Zone.js after async events.

questions.question: Dozens of Vue components share cart state through one central store that enforces updates via mutations and actions rather than an event bus. Which library is this?
questions.explanation: Vuex is Vue's classic centralized state store enforcing unidirectional flow through mutations and actions; Pinia is the modern successor without mutations.

questions.question: Cart transitions (ADD_ITEM, REMOVE_ITEM, CLEAR) multiply, so the dev centralizes them in a pure (state, action) function invoked via dispatch. Which React hook manages this?
questions.explanation: useReducer manages state with a Redux-style reducer, making complex multi-action transitions predictable and testable.

questions.question: An Angular search box emits each keystroke as a stream the component subscribes to with RxJS operators like debounceTime. What reactive primitive carries the stream?
questions.explanation: Observables are RxJS's lazy push-based streams that subscribers consume over time with composable operators.

questions.question: In Vue 3's setup(), a dev makes a primitive counter reactive so `count.value++` triggers view updates. Which API creates it?
questions.explanation: ref() wraps a value in a reactive object accessed via .value; use reactive() for whole objects instead.

questions.question: A Vue dev wraps the whole cart object so nested `state.cart.items.push()` mutations trigger updates — no .value needed. Which API wraps the object?
questions.explanation: reactive() returns a deep Proxy of an object, tracking nested property access and mutation without unwrapping.

questions.question: A product row re-renders on every parent update though its props never change; the dev wraps the component in a higher-order API memoizing by props. Which API?
questions.explanation: React.memo memoizes a component's rendered output, skipping re-renders when props are shallowly equal.

questions.question: An Angular SPA maps /products/:id to components without full reloads, registered in the app module via `___.forRoot(routes)`. Which module fills the blank?
questions.explanation: RouterModule provides the directives (router-outlet, routerLink) and services that map URLs to components in Angular.

questions.question: Typing in a filter box must stay snappy while a huge list re-renders; the dev wraps the list update so React may interrupt it. Which hook marks updates non-urgent?
questions.explanation: useTransition/startTransition tags updates as low priority so React keeps urgent renders like typing responsive.

questions.question: Three components duplicate fetch + loading + error logic; the dev extracts it into a shared `useProducts()` function. What is useProducts?
questions.explanation: Custom hooks are functions starting with 'use' that reuse stateful logic across components without changing JSX.

questions.question: A Vue 3 dev organizes logic by feature inside setup() using ref() and computed() instead of data/methods option blocks. Which API style is this?
questions.explanation: The Composition API groups reactive logic by concern in setup() or <script setup>, replacing the scattered Options API layout.

questions.question: A Next.js marketing site wants HTML generated once at build time and served from a CDN with zero per-request rendering. Which rendering mode?
questions.explanation: Static Site Generation renders pages during the build, serving instant cached HTML for content that rarely changes.

questions.question: Product pages must stay static-fast yet refresh every 60 seconds with fresh prices — no full rebuild. Which Next.js feature revalidates them?
questions.explanation: ISR regenerates static pages in the background after a revalidate window, combining SSG speed with fresh data.

questions.question: After state changes, React diffs the new virtual DOM against the previous one to compute minimal real-DOM updates. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: Reconciliation is React's diffing algorithm that determines the smallest set of DOM mutations needed.

questions.question: A React developer fetches order data inside a hook that runs after render and can clean up on unmount. Which hook is it?
questions.explanation: useEffect runs side effects after render; its returned function acts as the cleanup.

questions.question: A Vue form uses one directive so an input and its data property stay synchronized both ways. Which directive?
questions.explanation: v-model creates two-way binding on form inputs, combining :value and @input.

questions.question: An Angular component receives HttpClient through its constructor instead of instantiating it. Which design pattern supplies the service?
questions.explanation: Angular's injector supplies declared dependencies, decoupling components from concrete instantiation.

questions.question: Cart state must be readable by many nested components without prop drilling, so the developer wraps the app in a provider. Which React feature is this?
questions.explanation: React Context broadcasts values to descendant consumers via a Provider, avoiding prop drilling.
